Sam: Quick capture cookbook for a short nsys run focused on KV-cache + batching hotspots. Throwing this here so folks have a consistent baseline to reproduce the regression.

Sam: Example I ran locally (short bracketed capture):
```
nsys profile \\
  --output out/kv_batch_probe.qdrep \\
  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \\
  --capture-range=nvtx \\
  --capture-range-start=kv_warmup_start \\
  --capture-range-end=kv_probe_end \\
  --duration=12s \\
  --sample=cpu
```

Sam: Notes: use NVTX markers around the exact forward-pass section you care about (prefix+batch) so the trace file stays small. 12s is usually enough for multiple requests with different seq lengths.

Maya: File-size question — how big does out.qdrep get with that? Any heuristics to keep it under ~200MB?

Sam: If you only trace cuda+nvtx+osrt and bracket tightly, we stay ~50-150MB depending on workload. If you forget bracket, we blow past 1GB in a minute.

Maya: Good call. Also do a short warmup then bracket — otherwise long tail idle kernels get captured and confuse kernel selection heuristics.

Jorge: For the KV cache regression I sliced the trace and focused on the kernel timeline: we saw a recurring small kernel (~sub-ms) that dominated scheduling overhead when batch > 24. Looks like a matmul fallback variant invoked by the runtime's kernel selector.

Jorge: Quick triage checklist I used:
- bracketed nsys capture (nvtx markers)
- compare two qdrep exports with nsys-ui or `nsys stats`
- look at kernel timeline: sort by total time and by invocation count
- check osrt markers for KV eviction events (we annotate them)

Sam: For reproducing kernel chooser issues, force a short deterministic run:
- set a fixed batch profile (e.g., 16/24/32)
- pin CPU/GPU freq to reduce jitter
- capture multiple warmup+measured windows (3x 10s)

Maya: Any thoughts on sampling vs continuous tracing? We used sampling to cut overhead but missed a tiny hotpath last week.

Sam: Tradeoffs: sampling (lower overhead) can miss brief, high-frequency microkernels. Continuous tracing (full cuda events) captures everything but file size and overhead jump. My rule: sampling for high-level hotspots; continuous for kernel selection/regression hunts.

ci-bot: Artifact uploaded: s3://ci-artifacts/kv_batch_probe/3456000000/kv_batch_probe.qdrep :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Reminder: large qdrep files older than 7 days will be moved to cold storage. If you need them for debugging, pin them in the bug ticket.

Maya: Observed in timeline: when batch >=32 the runtime picks a different matmul kernel (longer latency, fewer flops). Hypothesis: selector prefers memory-bound kernel when effective seq len large. Jorge, can you re-run with env var to force the matmul variant?

Jorge: Yup — forced variant via env REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=matmul_high_throughput and re-ran. Kernel spike resolved, latency steady. Will open a tiny repro with two captures attached.

Sam: Closing notes for the cookbook:
- Always NVTX-bracket your forward pass sections
- Start sampling to narrow big offenders, switch to continuous for kernel selection validation
- Use short durations (8-20s) and repeat runs to reduce noise
- Export CSVs from nsys-ui for quick compare: kernel name, total time, invocations
- Annotate KV cache ops with NVTX so you can correlate evictions to kernel spikes

Maya: Thanks — I'll add this to the perf runbook and link the repro ticket.
